## Findings
- claim-1: arXiv:0809.2981v2 formally states: for \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\) is generated as an ideal of \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by either \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) or \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [source-2@L1382-L1402|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The same source gives a general graded-module proposition over a commutative ring \(R\), then specializes to symmetric functions with \(\mathbb Z\)-coefficients and \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\). [source-2@L1522-L1540|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: The supplied arXiv excerpts do not state an equality identifying \(J_v\) as an exact integral \(\mathbb Z\)-span of a specified Schur family. The earlier definition instead says \(J_v:=\Bbbk\)-span of \(\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\), without specifying \(\Bbbk\) in that excerpt. [source-2@L328-L337|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: Provider metadata identifies the later paper as Avery St. Dizier and Alexander Yong, “Presenting the cohomology of a Schubert variety: Proof of the minimality conjecture,” DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\); its abstract says it proves the minimality conjecture using the Hopf-algebra structure of symmetric functions. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- claim-5: The retrieved later DOI and arXiv:2209.02011v2 records supply abstract-level material only; neither contains exact theorem text giving an integral Schur-span description of \(J_v\), nor precise coefficient hypotheses. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832] [arxiv:2209.02011v2]
- claim-6: No conclusion about the later paper’s exact theorem statement, its coefficient ring, or an integral Schur-span presentation follows from the retrieved abstracts.
## Strategy
Report only retrieved-record content: original excerpts give integral ideal generation and a \(\mathbb Z\)-module setup, but no exact integral Schur-span equality; later-paper records are metadata/abstract only.

## Gaps
No theorem-level full text was retrieved for DOI 10.1112/jlms.12832. Its exact theorem statement, coefficient ring, and any integral \(J_v\) Schur-span formulation remain unresolved. This does not assert their absence from the full paper.

## Next
Obtain indexed full-text theorem passages for the later paper before making any theorem-level claim.
